#1476. Montella describes ‘dream’ Milan opportunity, Berlusconi and the Supercoppa: “An incredible feeling”

Vincenzo Montella’s time with AC Milan was ‘a dream’ for him, but he failed to achieve much during his time at the helm.

Looking back on Montella’s time leading Milan is tricky. On paper, the Italian had a strong tenure at the club, achieving a 50% win rate and only losing 18 of his 64 games in charge at San Siro, not a terrible record by any means.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He even ended a five-year trophy drought with a win against Juventus in the Supercoppa Italiana and returned the Rossoneri to Europe, with a sixth-place finish in the 2016/17 season. In itself, that was a first since 2014.

This is where context matters, though. The start of the 2017/18 season was tough, as the Diavolo won six of their first 14 games and he was sacked before December. Despite that, he still views the club in an excellent light.

Speaking to La Gazzetta dello Sport’s ‘La Tripletta’ podcast, Montella went over his time with the club and how he fulfilled a dream by taking the job, as MilanPress relays.

“It was a fantastic experience there [at Milan] too, it was my dream. Then, as a professional, it’s a little different, but when I was thirteen I was a fan of that AC Milan team. My older brother took me to see Maradona’s Napoli team twice to make me a Napoli fan, and Maradona scored three goals.

“Despite this, my idol was Van Basten because I was a striker: I studied him and dreamed of becoming like him, and so I was a Milan fan. I knew everything about Milan, so for me it was an incredible feeling to join Milan.”

“He liked to talk about football; he liked to give advice even when it was a bit out of context at the time, because he always had the mentality of having Van Basten as a centre forward with Papin, a two-time Ballon d’Or winner, on the bench. He wanted me to play with two strikers, and I tried to plug the gap for months.

“I told him it was difficult; I knew all the lineups of those years. I was a Milan fan: the starter was Van Basten and the reserve was Papin, both Ballon d’Or winners. So, ‘If you buy me some players like that, rest assured that I’ll play them both.'”

“It was a year when we returned to Europe. I think it had been two or three years since Milan had been there, and it was something new at the time. We won a trophy, a small one. Just the other night I saw Galliani at a dinner; he reminded me of it and remembers it perfectly.

“I have to say that I found him to be the perfect manager at the time, because he was always on my side when it came to pressure; he gave me complete autonomy in my decisions and he helped me with everything, from the number of collaborators to new things; whatever I asked for, he was always on the coach’s side.

“And so for me he was truly an incredible manager, who in that phase, in that change, was fundamental even in achieving these small results, especially after Berlusconi’s great AC Milan.

“We deserved to win even in regulation time: we had some easy chances to win it, then it came to penalties. Gigio saved the penalty from Dybala, who kicked it really hard, but he filled the net with it.”

“I was a little worried from the beginning because there was this obsession with publicising everything, almost like a publicity stunt, so I was a little worried. In theory, there was sharing, at least that’s what it looked like, but I couldn’t back out when in reality that wasn’t always the case.

“And so sometimes there were players I hadn’t even consulted about, who would arrive and then say, ‘It was shared,’ and when you’re there, you can’t say otherwise. Certainly, when you build a team and have the budget, the first thing you do is: we had a goalkeeper, I’ll get a centre forward, we were missing a centre forward.

“In the final selection, the centre forward was the only one left, with a budget of 15-20 million. And then Kalinic… yes, I chose him because that was the final budget. So our, let’s say, second-choice striker was paid thirty-eight million, if I remember correctly, who was André Silva, and the first striker was paid half that.

“And so, in my opinion, a misunderstanding of this kind was created, with so many changes, even though at that stage we weren’t even playing badly for having fifteen new players.

“We still had Calhanoglu, who wasn’t feeling well, coming off months of suspension. The team was still being built: we weren’t in line with the Scudetto objectives that had been announced, but certainly, given our development, we were absolutely on target.

“Who would I have signed up front? At the time, we were probably negotiating for Aubameyang, if I remember correctly. Ronaldo? No, I didn’t believe it, not at all.”

#1475. Hull reignite genuine survival hopes with late Oli McBurnie double to down Brighton, as talk of Seagulls emulating Leicester City-style fairytale is made to look foolish

Published: 12:04 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:08 EST, 23 November 2026

When Brighton owner Tony Bloom was asked about his club’s title prospects last week, he suggested they could emulate Leicester City’s 2015-16 fairytale and win the Premier League.

It was a bold claim, yet Fabian Hurzeler’s men looked anything but title aspirants after being downed by Oli McBurnie’s dramatic late double for newly-promoted Hull City.

Brighton have been the most credible challengers to Arsenal so far this season. That cannot be denied.

With Manchester City wobbling alarmingly, and the rest of the traditional big guns largely off the title pace, the Seagulls have at least given Mikel Arteta’s champions something to think about.

But this bitterly cold afternoon in East Yorkshire was a reality check for Hurzeler’s men and a harsh lesson in taking the chances that come your way.

Brighton didn’t and McBurnie most certainly did, firing home clinically from close range twice in added time shortly after Joao Costinha had been sent off.

Oli McBurnie scored a late brace to secure a brilliant three points for Hull against Brighton

McBurnie has made a habit of leaving it late – the rejuvenated Scotland striker struck a 95th-minute winner in the Championship play-off final against Middlesbrough at Wembley in May.

Hull had gone eight Premier League games without a win before Brighton’s visit and this success lifted them to 11th.

Tigers boss Sergej Jakirovic said of McBurnie: 'I’ve never had any doubts over a ‘Braveheart’ like Oli because he’s a natural leader and very important for us.'

Asked where the setback left Brighton’s title hopes, Hurzeler said: 'We don’t focus on the table – we focus on performances and how we can make the right improvements into the team.

'That’s the same if we had won or lost, but today showed there are still things we need to do better. That’s what we will do and then see what the outcome will be.'

Brighton arrived as favourites and could have cut Arsenal's lead at the top of the table

Hull were indebted to a remarkable display from their Greek goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, who reduced Brighton to an afternoon of frustration and futility.

The visitors had 10 attempts at goal during the first half alone, forcing Hull’s summer signing into a string of fine saves and also being denied by the woodwork.

At times the Seagulls’ pretty patterns threatened to cut the Tigers apart as the likes of Maxim De Cuyper, Diego Gomez and the effervescent Pascal Gross – on his 300th appearance for the club – knitted them together superbly.

Georginio Rutter was involved in a move which saw De Cuyper cross low from the left flank to the onrushing Gomez, whose close-range effort was superbly saved by Tzolakis.

That set the tone for an outstanding display by the 24-year-old Greece international, who arrived in the summer from Olympiacos as part of the newly-promoted Tigers’ £150million spending spree which saw 18 players signed.

Hull lacked nothing in spirit and fight but Brighton had the quality and constantly threatened to open up their hosts.

As half-time approached, Rutter saw a close-range shot repelled by Tzolakis after Yasin Ayari’s effort rebounded off the crossbar.

The Tigers were constantly grateful to their goalkeeper, who made another save to keep out an effort from Gomez on the stroke of half-time.

Tzolakis continued to prove unbeatable in the second half too, and his opposite number Bart Verbruggen was left grateful to the woodwork after a cross-shot from substitute Sorba Thomas hit the crossbar.

Mohamed Belloumi was also a lingering threat for Hull on the right flank and he should have scored after cutting infield before firing wastefully wide.

Konstantinos Tzolakis (right) produced a remarkable display to keep Brighton out

As the game wore on, there was an inescapable feeling that Brighton could be punished for their wastefulness as Hull showed the kind of courage which deserves, and usually gets, its rewards.

Regan Slater cleared a shot from Charalampos Kostoulas off the line before Brighton lost Joao Costinha to a second yellow card with a minute remaining.

The Tigers sensed blood, pouring forward to lead in the first minute of added time as McBurnie expertly sidefooted them in front from Lucas Gourna-Douath’s neat pass to cap a delightful flowing move.

Moments before the final whistle, Hull struck again as McBurnie swept home from close range again from Mo Belloumi’s assist. Cue delirium in the home stands.

McBurnie took the acclaim but Tzolakis was Hull’s star man as Jakirovic acknowledged: 'Tzolakis was amazing and we could have been two or three-nil down without his saves.

'We stayed alive because of him and then won the game at the end. Ciao!'

Hull had failed to win since beating Manchester United and Coventry in their opening two games in August.

Hull reignited their survival hopes with a precious win against an in-form team

Crucially, however, they have been competitive in every game this season and are now unbeaten in six home matches.

Can they survive? 'Of course, and every win is so important,' declared Jakirovic.

'I wish this feeling I have now would never stop but I know how demanding this league is.'

#1474. Alonso ready to sell £47m Chelsea signing for a Barca star

Chelsea transfer news: Xabi Alonso wants Barcelona right-back Jules Koundé at Chelsea and is ready to sell Marco Palestra, his £47m summer signing, to make room, according to El Nacional. The outlet says Alonso has pushed the case, a claim it credits to FourFourTwo, and that Palestra has Serie A interest from Juventus, AC Milan and Napoli, though it mentions no bid.

Barcelona would reportedly listen to offers of around €50m, roughly £43m, because Hansi Flick doesn’t treat Koundé as untouchable. The 28-year-old has started three of six LaLiga games this season after an ankle sprain on 17 October kept him out for over a month. El Nacional calls him a backup behind Eric García and says he’d welcome the move.

Koundé completes 93.9% of his passes, wins 58.8% of his duels and has 58 France caps, a composed defender who could play right-back or on the right of a back three. His body is the worry: a hamstring problem in March, then an ankle injury that lingered.

Palestra won Serie A’s Defender of the Year award at Cagliari, and his 81 completed dribbles topped every defender in Europe’s top five leagues. A thigh injury delayed his Chelsea debut until October, and El Nacional puts him at 202 minutes across six matches. Alonso prefers Josh Acheampong at right-back and, per BBC Sport, uses Palestra from the bench before Malo Gusto. He scored once in 37 league games, and his crossing remains modest.

Not as a swap. Palestra is a wing-back who beats opponents on the outside, while Koundé is a passer and cover defender best placed on the right of three centre-backs. Selling one doesn’t remove the need for the other, and Chelsea’s real shortage is right-sided cover: Reece James is injured and has been used in midfield, and Acheampong, a centre-back by trade, is filling in at right-back.

Koundé would solve that, but Gusto is the sale to make. He has lost his place, is reportedly open to a January exit, and Chelsea priced him at £75m in June, so even a discounted fee would cover much of Koundé’s £43m.

Selling Palestra after 202 minutes would mean writing off a player Alonso recruited and said needs time to adapt, to buy a 28-year-old with a muscle-injury record. Chelsea were fifth, 11 points behind Arsenal, before Leeds visited, without European football. Buy Koundé if the medical is clean, sell Gusto and keep Palestra.

#1472. Liverpool track Swedish left-back with £38m price tag

Liverpool transfer news: Liverpool are tracking Borussia Dortmund left-back Daniel Svensson, according to fussball-news.de, which names them and Arsenal as the most interested clubs.

Manchester United, Leeds, Milan, Juventus, Inter and Real Madrid are also watching the 24-year-old. Liverpool and Milan are reportedly preparing concrete steps for the winter window, although the report attributes no bid to either.

Dortmund will not make it easy. They want to keep a player contracted until June 2029 and plan to raise his salary, while Svensson feels settled and has no wish for a rushed move. A sale would cost at least €45m (about £38m), and Premier League clubs are ready to test Dortmund with a €30m (roughly £25m) offer, yet FotMob values him at just €23m.

The numbers explain the interest. Svensson has started all 10 Bundesliga games this season. His expected assists total of 1.13 comes without a single assist, and he has made 22 tackles, 14 interceptions and 45 recoveries while passing at 86.1%. He can play in midfield.

The flaws are clear. He has won only eight of 29 aerial duels and landed six of 32 crosses. He also plays as a wing-back in front of a back three, so Andoni Iraola’s back four would ask him to defend more of the flank alone.

Iraola’s 4-2-3-1 sends full-backs forward, and Milos Kerkez, bought for a reported £40m last year, has no goals or assists in the Premier League this season. Kostas Tsimikas, 30, is the backup on a contract that expires next year.

Not in January, and not at €45m. A €30m offer would fail, and £38m for a player FotMob values at €23m is poor business. Summer 2027 is the realistic window, once Tsimikas’s deal has run down.

The bigger problem sits on the other flank. Ronald Araujo, a centre-back by trade, is filling in at right-back while injuries have hit that position all season, so Iraola needs a natural right-back more urgently than a second left-back. Kerkez is 22 and signed until 2030, so Svensson would challenge him rather than replace him, which is healthy given Kerkez’s lack of end product.

Kerkez arrived with two Premier League seasons behind him, while Svensson would have to adapt to a new league and a new system. Liverpool should buy a right-back first and hold a ceiling of around £35m for Svensson, because above that they would repeat the Kerkez gamble with less evidence.

#1471. Juventus boss reacts to Manchester United’s midfield link: Is he worth £28m?

Tuttomercato carries Luciano Spalletti’s reaction to the talk linking Weston McKennie with Manchester United, and the Juventus head coach played it down. He spoke to the midfielder as soon as the story broke and didn’t think McKennie had hinted at wanting to leave, calling his comments a general remark. Spalletti said their relationship is as good as the one he has with everybody else, and everything felt calm once McKennie returned from international duty.

Those comments came from McKennie himself, who suggested during USMNT camp that Mauricio Pochettino could bring American players to Old Trafford. La Gazzetta dello Sport then reported that United’s new head coach wants him in January, though McKennie says he isn’t planning to leave and Fabrizio Romano insists United aren’t working on a deal.

Pochettino inherits a club in trouble: one win and eight points from ten league games, 18th place and Michael Carrick’s sacking after their worst league start in 40 years. The Argentine takes charge at Anfield today, before Wednesday’s Champions League trip to Sporting CP.

McKennie, 28, offers versatility: Spalletti has used him on both wings, at wing-back and even as a striker, and he managed eight goals and five assists in 38 appearances before signing his new deal in March. This season the output has dipped, with FotMob showing one goal, no assists and a 6.98 rating from eight Serie A starts. His contract runs to 2030, and FotMob values him at about £28m.

Not as a January priority. United’s problem is a team that loses control of matches, and McKennie is a runner who arrives in the box rather than a midfielder who dictates tempo. Put him next to a struggling back four and his versatility becomes a drawback, because Spalletti gets the best from him higher up the pitch, where his goals come from.

Pochettino’s trust is a real advantage, since he knows exactly what work rate he gets, but trust doesn’t turn a 28-year-old with one league goal this season into a £28m solution to a defensive crisis. Juventus also just rewarded him with a contract to 2030, so they have no reason to sell cheaply.

Romano mentioned Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos in the same breath, and each offers more control from midfield. If Pochettino wants a familiar face, a rotation option on a short deal makes sense. Spending about £28m on a runner does not.

#1470. Tottenham join race for Inter midfielder facing pay cut: Right move for Spurs?

Tottenham transfer news: Tottenham Hotspur are one of four clubs tracking Hakan Calhanoglu, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The Italian outlet lists Galatasaray, Juventus and Como alongside Spurs, although it gives no detail on how far Tottenham’s interest has progressed.

The timing matters because the Inter midfielder’s contract expires on 30 June 2027, which lets him agree a pre-contract with a foreign club from January. Inter want to extend but are trimming wages for their over-30s. Calhanoglu earns roughly £5.7m a year, and Inter are discussing £4.4m plus bonuses. He prefers to stay but hopes to avoid a heavy cut, and no formal offer exists yet.

Calhanoglu turns 33 in February. FotMob shows three goals in 485 minutes from nine Serie A appearances, 91.4% pass accuracy, 20 chances created and a 98th-percentile ranking for shot attempts among Serie A central midfielders.

Passing range, long-distance shooting and dead-ball quality remain his strengths. He wins only 44.4% of his duels, though, completes a quarter of his dribbles, and his recovery speed will keep dropping with age. FotMob values him at about £6.4m, down from a £39m peak in 2024.

Roberto De Zerbi wants his midfield to dictate play from deep, which suits Calhanoglu’s skills. Spurs have 15 points from 11 league games after beating Ipswich 2-0 on Saturday, their fourth win in five. Yet Sandro Tonali (£100m) and Mateus Fernandes (£85m) joined in July, and Rodrigo Bentancur, Conor Gallagher and Archie Gray compete for the same places.

Not as a priority. Money isn’t the obstacle. Tonali reportedly earns more than £275,000 a week, so Calhanoglu’s wages would barely register, and a free transfer costs no fee. Squad space is the problem. Spurs bought Tonali and Fernandes to run De Zerbi’s base for years, and a 33-year-old in the same role would either sit on the bench or take minutes from Gray and Lucas Bergvall, whom the club needs to develop.

Spurs would also struggle to sell the project without European football, while Galatasaray can reportedly offer higher wages. The case only strengthens if Tonali or Bentancur leaves, or if De Zerbi wants a penalty and set-piece specialist. Neither applies now, and nothing forces Spurs to act in January.

Calhanoglu’s output is real, but it comes with a decline in athleticism that a 33-year-old can’t reverse. Spurs would be paying for a short-term fix in a position where they have already invested £185m in the long-term answer.

#1468. How Amorim picked apart Alvini’s gung-ho approach: Tactical analysis of AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone

AC Milan put on arguably their best display of the Ruben Amorim era so far as they beat Frosinone 5-1 at San Siro on Sunday.

Gabriele Calvani’s early own-goal kicked off what would be a miserable night for the Canarini, before Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. Patrizio Masini’s goal halved the deficit, and kept the game open going into the second half.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

From there, though, the Rossoneri ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both scored within minutes of coming off the bench, finishing counter-attacks, then Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

It was a win that Milan needed to move back into the top four, also given that only Inter out of the top six sides in the table dropped points. Rohit Rajeev has the tactical breakdown from the win.

Ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

Milan once again deployed a modified version of their 3-4-2-1, with Bartesaghi operating on the left. Alvini, meanwhile, had to cope without his striker Raimondo and opted for a 3-5-2, pairing Ghedjemis and Kvernadze up front.

Frosinone made their intentions clear from the opening seconds. Goalkeeper Palmisani immediately played a direct ball into a targeted zone, with Frosinone committing several players towards the expected landing area to create a numerical advantage and win the aerial duel.

Milan built from deep with three players at the back, while Maignan pushed forward to act as an additional centre-back. This created a 4v3 in the first line of build-up, forcing Frosinone’s front three of Ghedjemis, Kvernadze and Schmid to press deeper.

Their movement opened up space between Frosinone’s first and second pressing lines for Milan’s players to receive.

Milan built from deep with three players at the back, while Maignan pushed forward to act as an additional centre-back. This created a 4v3 in the first line of build-up, forcing Frosinone’s front three of Ghedjemis, Kvernadze and Schmid to press deeper. Their movement opened up space between Frosinone’s first and second pressing lines for Milan’s players to receive. However, it was Rabiot’s movement that proved decisive in creating the overload for Milan’s opening goal. With Frosinone committing three forwards to the press and keeping two players wide, only two midfielders and three defenders remained to deal with Milan’s build-up. Although Musah and Rabiot were initially marked, Rabiot dropped deeper into midfield to create a numerical advantage and free himself to receive possession.

— Rohit Rajeev (@keralista) November 23, 2026

However, it was Rabiot’s movement that proved decisive in creating the overload for Milan’s opening goal. With Frosinone committing three forwards to the press and keeping two players wide, only two midfielders and three defenders remained to deal with Milan’s build-up.

Although Musah and Rabiot were initially marked, Rabiot dropped deeper into midfield to create a numerical advantage and free himself to receive possession.

This movement directly contributed to Milan’s opening goal. Rabiot dropped between the lines to receive possession, forcing Cittadini to step out of his defensive position and follow him.

Rabiot then laid the ball off to Modric, who immediately played it into the space vacated by Cittadini. Under pressure, Frosinone inadvertently turned the ball into their own net to give Milan a 1-0 lead.

Frosinone looked to commit numbers into Milan’s half, creating ball-sided overloads to progress through the pitch. Their two wingers maintained wide positions to stretch Milan’s wing-backs and create more space in the central areas.

Out of possession, Frosinone adopted a 3-4-3 to match Milan’s 3-4-2-1 in possession. They also maintained a very high defensive line, looking to press Milan aggressively and win the ball back as high up the pitch as possible.

Milan allowed Frosinone to dictate possession, dropping into a deeper defensive block to invite them into their half. Once Frosinone advanced, Milan looked to win the ball back and launch quick counter-attacks.

Frosinone’s lack of a clear attacking structure and, more importantly, an organised rest defence left them vulnerable in transition. Milan exploited this disorganisation repeatedly, with the next four goals all benefiting from the spaces Frosinone left behind.

The second goal perfectly illustrated Milan’s approach in transition. Frosinone had committed ten players into Milan’s half, leaving very little defensive cover behind.

Ramos won possession, and Musah immediately played a vertical pass to release Moreira through on goal. Moreira and Rabiot then drew three recovering defenders towards them before creating the space for Ramos to finish.

Frosinone’s high-risk approach briefly paid off with Masini’s goal. They drew Milan into central areas before pressing aggressively to recover possession. With their players positioned close together, they were able to combine quickly and progress the ball towards Kvernadze.

A deflection off De Winter then took the ball into Ghedjemis’ path, allowing him to set up Masini for the finish.

Frosinone consistently targeted Milan’s left flank, particularly the space around Bartesaghi. The individual duel between Ghedjemis and Bartesaghi became a key feature of the game.

Ghedjemis repeatedly beat his marker in 1v1 situations and posed a threat. Recognising the problem, Amorim took Bartesaghi off at half-time.

After the break, Jashari and Pulisic began making coordinated counter-movements. Pulisic dropped deeper, drawing his marker away and creating space in the wide attacking area, which Jashari then exploited with an advancing run.

The goal was very similar to the movement Jashari made against Venezia, highlighting a recurring pattern in Milan’s attacking play.

Both Cisse’s and Pulisic’s goals came from a counter-attack following a Frosinone corner, for which they did not leave many men back.

For Cisse’s finish, his body orientation suggested he was going to shoot towards the goalkeeper’s right, prompting the keeper to adjust his stance accordingly. Cisse then went the other way, finding the opposite corner.

⚽️ GOAL ALPHADJO CISSE! 🔥 https://t.co/aMIgE9PXHc

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 22, 2026

Pulisic, meanwhile, used the bridge of his foot to execute a delicate chip, lifting the ball over the advancing goalkeeper and completing the counter-attack.

⚽️ GOAL CHRISTIAN PULISIC 🇺🇸 https://t.co/B4mP55RJ8u

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 22, 2026

We wrote something during the break about how Milan are over-performing relative to certain metrics. Above all, their actual goals scored was/is well above their Expected Goals, helped by the fact four players are converting an abnormally high percentage of chances.

With this in mind, the stats make for interesting reading. Milan edged possession with 54%, generating 2.50 Expected Goals, so they again out-performed what they created. And yet, the Rossoneri racked up five big chances which matches the number of goals scored.

So, perhaps everything can be taken with a pinch of whatever type of salt fits your narrative. Many would argue that Milan could have scored more given their brilliant on Sunday, yet xG would have you believe it was a ‘lucky’ margin in a game that should have been 2/3-1.

The visitors also racked up nine corners, the most Milan have conceded all season, but thankfully Amorim’s side managed to deal with them all relatively well.

#1467. Manchester City’s £31m left-back wanted in Turin: Loan or sale in January?

CalcioMercato reports that Juventus have started monitoring Rayan Aït-Nouri ahead of the transfer market reopening, and the Manchester City left-back seems ready to listen. The Algeria international wants to restart his career elsewhere, views Turin favourably and has told his entourage to strengthen contacts, while the interest from Juventus is real and the club intends to act soon to test the deal’s feasibility.

City want to sell outright and reinvest immediately, whereas Juventus prefer a loan with an option to buy, which suits a club bound by a UEFA settlement agreement. They first asked in August and City refused, while Gazzetta dello Sport says Luciano Spalletti wants competition for Andrea Cambiaso.

City paid Wolves a reported £31m in June 2025 and gave him a contract until 2030, yet Enzo Maresca reportedly ranks the 25-year-old behind Joško Gvardiol and Nico O’Reilly. He had played 168 minutes in all competitions by mid-November, none of them in the Premier League, and his only starts have come in the EFL Cup.

His strengths explain the fee. Aït-Nouri scored nine goals and set up 15 in 135 Premier League games for Wolves, added five assists in 1,605 minutes last season, and can also operate in central areas.

The weakness is defensive security, because he is an ultra-attacking left-back. That matters now, with City on one point from their last four league games after losing 3-1 at Nottingham Forest and drawing 1-1 with Fulham on Saturday.

No, not in January, and not on terms that leave City carrying all the risk. Maresca has used Nico O’Reilly in midfield this season, yet O’Reilly started only seven of City’s first 15 games while managing a back problem, so an available specialist left-back is no luxury. Khusanov, Nunes and Guéhi all picked up knocks at Forest, which leaves the back line short.

City should treat the Juventus talks as a pricing exercise. A straight loan sends a 25-year-old on a contract until 2030 away for six months and returns him no more valuable, so only a loan with an obligation to buy close to the £31m fee makes sense.

Otherwise, give him a league start, see whether his attacking threat helps a side that keeps conceding, and let Maresca’s evidence decide. A club that paid £31m for a left-back last year has not shown he cannot do the job; it has shown only that the manager prefers somebody else.

#1466. Lethal Trent Alexander-Arnold sends Tuchel a statement in England victory

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

England always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the new half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24

Will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

Having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the big delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

“I make that run time and time again,” Gordon said of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”

A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

As for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

“Strange to get an early red card,” Tuchel said. “Not the best for the team and spectators. It’s an awkward one, but we kept going, got a win and that’s what counts.” Not quite a vintage Czech Republic team, either, and when their best player of the opening stages, the attacking midfielder Pavel Sulc, of Lyon in Ligue 1, was dismissed after 25 minutes, it certainly did not become any easier for the home team. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. It was high on the right calf of the England midfielder.

Czech Republic DOWN TO 10 MEN! 🟥Pavel Šulc sees red for a dangerous challenge on Elliot Anderson#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/B2YOLuS0vL

England had looked once more a little open to the counter-attack in the early stages, with Sulc one notable runner. This was not an opponent of the quality of Spain and Tuchel’s players were able to recover the situation. When they lose the ball in the opposition’s half, England tend to look vulnerable.

Even before the red card Rogers had hit a post. Myles Lewis-Skelly, playing in midfield, was booked for a foul on Lukas Serv and was pursued thereafter by the Czech players hoping to get an upgrade on the yellow card. He was substituted at half-time, with Eberechi Eze on in his place.

“I spoke to Ant [Gordon] at half-time,” Alexander-Arnold said later to ITV, “and I said if I’m getting in those spaces make sure you get to the back post. You don’t expect to get it that fast, but it did and it worked.”

Two minutes after the break, Alexander-Arnold suddenly burst into life. He won the ball back in his own area and then drove forward in search of the return. When that did not come, he raced back to win the ball again and unleashed one of those right-footed outswingers to the back post, where Gordon guided in the header. “Really proud to score that,” Gordon said, “because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.”

Kane scored the second just a minute before he was replaced and Bellingham took the captain’s armband and the role as a No 9. One day someone will have to step into those goalscorer’s boots on a permanent basis and try to replace Kane – although it may be a while yet.

Thomas Tuchel has backed Jude Bellingham as a future England captain after giving him the armband in the victory over the Czech Republic.

In the absence of Declan Rice, who was vice-captain at the World Cup, Bellingham assumed the role when he came on for Harry Kane, who is now in his 10th season as England captain and also scored in the 2-0 win in Prague.

Tuchel, who needs to check on Bellingham ahead of Saturday’s game against Croatia after a “niggle,” has praised the midfielder’s attitude during the extended international break one year after he was back from an injury but left out of the squad.

“If you are the captain at the end of these matches, you can be the permanent captain,” Tuchel said when asked whether Bellingham could eventually lead the team. “He was the captain against New Zealand before the World Cup. It is always a reward and always an honour.

“I think he loves to be with us at the moment. That’s what I feel, and we had this small talk today about his role. We felt in our hearts or our stomachs to say ‘let’s go again, let’s start again’ and also our heads told us maybe 30 minutes is enough for this match because he hasn’t played in this quick turnaround through this season. He has done it before, but not in the season, so we didn’t want to be the first ones to try that.

“But even in this little encounter, you can see that he’s confident and happy to help from the bench. So it’s a reward. It’s good. He had a little niggle at the end of the match, so hopefully it’s nothing serious, and he’s available for Croatia.”

Nico O’Reilly is a doubt for the Croatia match in Rijeka and there are also concerns over Ezri Konsa, who was on the bench but not fit enough to play.

Trent Alexander-Arnold provided an assist for Anthony Gordon in the Real Madrid full-back’s first cap in 15 months. Gordon, meanwhile, has now scored in the first two Nations League games of the campaign and is staking his case to be an indispensable player for Tuchel.

“He’s getting there. He’s defending his shirt, he’s defending his position, an excellent performance again after his performance against Spain,” Tuchel said.

“He was very decisive today and had an excellent goal. It was very, very difficult, but the technique and finishing was excellent. He scored against Spain, so he has decisive actions and he’s defending his shirt and his position. He does it on the highest level and he’s a very important player.”

England returned to winning ways with a 2-0 win over Czech Republic in Prague.

Pavel Sulc’s first-half red card after a VAR review of his clumsy challenge on Elliot Anderson took the sting out of the initially lively hosts and Anthony Gordon gave Thomas Tuchel’s men a deserved lead early in the second half.

The forward headed home a fantastic cross by Trent Alexander-Arnold, who was making his first start under the German coach, before skipper Harry Kane scored to settle any nerves.

So who played well for England and who failed to impress? Rate each player with our voting tool, and have your say in the comments.

I knew exactly where I wanted to go, where I needed to go but I needed some guidance. I think the same way as him [Jude]. We don’t think there’s any limit on what we can achieve, wanting to win, wanting to win in a good way by going for the throat. Fearlessness.

It ate me up for a good couple of weeks after [losing the semi-final]. I’d scored… on the same pitch as Messi, the man I idolised as a kid. It was the highest possible moment of my entire life. And within 20 minutes it had come completely crashing down. There’s been a lot of controversy, a lot of talk about that. Going forward, if we are going to lose a game, it’s going to be like how we lost to Spain. We went for their throats, we missed a penalty and lost the game. But the way we went for them, no regrets. I want to stay as far away from that [regret] as possible.

[Did you ever think you would sign for Barcelona?] Yes. No one ever achieves anything in life by playing it safe. My personality is based on being bold, taking risks and going for whatever you want.

At this level we’re all as talented as each other but only the most mentally competitive and driven people can maintain success for a long time.

I always thought in England that people respected me because I was fast and I pressed but they never respected my quality and people are starting to take notice that I’m not just quick. In Barcelona if you’re not technical, if you’re not smart, you’d stand out like a sore thumb.

[Where do you see this squad in two years?] European champions.

The intensity we played with and the way we took it to the best team in the world [is what we’ve taken out of the Spain game]. We can be really proud of that. It was really good. Obviously tight margins decide games but overall we’re happy with the way we dusted the World Cup off and all that emotion.

Massively [relishing a run in the No 10 position in place of Bellingham]. I want to try and show what I can do in that role and make a positive impact.

The atmosphere here [is always intense] and they have a new coach. We’ve done our research. We have to respect them. It’s going to be difficult and it’s up to us to hold our nerve.

The Professional Footballers’ Association has leapt to Cole Palmer’s defence following his withdrawal from the England squad.

The union’s CEO,  Maheta Molango, said the Chelsea forward is a victim of a “sick” system that is demanding too much from players physically.

“When England see five players who need to withdraw when the single most proud moment a player has is to be called up for the national team, you just ask yourself, what’s wrong about the industry?” Molango said at the Fifpro performance summit in London.

“You see people like Cole Palmer, someone who would have played four consecutive summers in a row had he gone to the World Cup, and you wonder why is he missing?”He’s missing because he’s a victim of the calendar and that’s something that needs to absolutely trigger the alarm bells.”

Man City used ‘sham’ sponsorships in £830m cheating scheme

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

#1465. Jose Mourinho sends clear Real Madrid message to Eder Militao and Antonio Rudiger after PSV double substitution

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 19:56

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has offered a revealing assessment of his defensive hierarchy after substituting Eder Militao and Antonio Rudiger at half-time during Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven.

Los Blancos were trailing 1-0 at the Santiago Bernabeu when Mourinho made three changes at the interval, withdrawing both experienced centre-backs alongside Aurelien Tchouameni. Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen entered in defence, while Jude Bellingham replaced the French midfielder.

The decision preceded a remarkable turnaround. Madrid scored five unanswered goals in the second half, with Bellingham, Federico Valverde, Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Junior contributing to a victory that maintained their perfect Champions League record after five matches.

Although Mourinho insisted that the improvement was primarily down to a collective change in mentality, his explanation for replacing Militao and Rudiger offered an insight into why Konate and Huijsen have established themselves as his preferred central-defensive partnership.

The Portuguese coach acknowledged that the two younger defenders currently benefit from greater match sharpness, while identifying specific qualities that make them particularly valuable to his system.

Speaking to Movistar after the match, Mourinho explained that his decision had been influenced by several factors, including the yellow cards shown to Rudiger and Tchouameni during the opening period.

"A bit of everything," he said when asked whether the substitutions were motivated by fitness, disciplinary concerns or a desire to change the game.

"We had two players on yellow cards in a game against some very quick players, which was a risk."

However, Mourinho's subsequent assessment was arguably more significant for the two defenders who had been withdrawn.

"Obviously, the two centre-backs who have been playing more regularly are in a better rhythm," he continued.

"Dean is our best player at bringing the ball out from the back, Konate is playing pretty well... and I thought those changes could help us."

Those comments underline the advantages currently enjoyed by Huijsen and Konate, who have become Mourinho's regular pairing since the beginning of the campaign.

Huijsen's ability to progress possession from defence is particularly important in a Madrid side expected to dominate the ball, while Konate provides the physical presence and defensive intensity required when the team presses high.

Both qualities were evident in the second half against PSV, when Madrid pushed their defensive line forward and prevented the Dutch visitors from progressing comfortably through midfield.

Mourinho nevertheless resisted the suggestion that his defensive substitutions alone had transformed the contest.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United manager also credited Bellingham's introduction and a collective improvement in pressing, explaining that his players had struggled to win individual battles before the interval.

"The second half was a question of mentality," Mourinho said. "We made changes, yes, and Jude is a different kind of player who gives us what we lacked in the first half, but collectively we were better in the second half."

His explanation makes it difficult to interpret the removal of Militao and Rudiger as an outright rejection of either player. Yet publicly highlighting the superior rhythm and individual qualities of their competitors offers a clear indication of the current pecking order.

The situation is particularly delicate for Rudiger, whose contract expires in June 2027.

The 33-year-old German has found regular opportunities difficult to secure under Mourinho, and reports in Spain have suggested that Real Madrid are increasingly unlikely to offer him another extension.

His experience remains an asset, particularly across a demanding season involving several competitions, but his reduced role raises questions about whether he will remain at the Bernabeu beyond next summer.

The Brazil international remains under contract until June 2028, although his recent career has been disrupted by two serious anterior cruciate ligament injuries and further muscular problems.

He has played only five minutes in La Liga this season, with his Champions League appearances providing most of his opportunities to regain competitive sharpness.

Tuesday's meeting with PSV represented another chance to demonstrate his readiness for a more prominent role. Instead, his involvement ended after 45 minutes as Mourinho turned to the partnership that has largely carried Madrid's defence this season.

The Brazilian's limited playing time makes the manager's comments about rhythm particularly relevant. Regaining his previous level requires regular appearances, but those opportunities are difficult to obtain while Konate and Huijsen continue to perform.

Huijsen's emergence has already complicated Militao's attempts to recover a starting place, with the Spain international establishing himself as a central figure in Mourinho's defensive plans.

Konate, meanwhile, has made a strong impression following his arrival from Liverpool, offering the combination of athleticism and defensive aggression that the Portuguese coach values.

The two established internationals therefore face different uncertainties. Rudiger must consider his future as his contract approaches its conclusion, while Militao has more time remaining on his deal but needs to demonstrate that he can compete consistently for a starting position.

Mourinho has not announced plans to sell either defender, and Tuesday's substitutions should not be regarded as confirmation of their departures.

However, the manager's unusually explicit assessment of his centre-backs has reinforced the challenge facing both players: Konate and Huijsen currently possess the match rhythm, tactical qualities and established partnership that make them difficult to displace.

#1464. Arsenal eye Serie A’s 11-goal striker: Should they pay £26m?

Arsenal transfer news from Italy centres on Monza striker Gustavo Varela, with Gianluca Di Marzio reportingthat the Gunners are very interested. The 21-year-old Portugal forward has scored 11 goals in 11 Serie A games since joining from Benfica B in July. Barcelona are equally keen, Inter watch him live at every match, and Napoli are reported as his strongest Italian suitor.

The interest makes sense. Viktor Gyokeres, signed for £64m in 2025, has two goals in 15 appearances and none in the Premier League, while Kai Havertz has started 10 of 11 league games for three goals. Arsenal’s results haven’t suffered, but their number nine position has produced little.

Finishing is the selling point. FotMob‘s data has him scoring well above his expected goals for a Monza side that won only two of its first 10 league games, and he averages around three shots per 90 minutes. The weaknesses are just as clear: he wins 34% of his duels, completes 41% of his dribbles and ranks in the ninth percentile among forwards for defensive contribution, which clashes with the pressing Arteta wants from his striker.

Di Marzio says Monza will listen at around £22m to £26m, with the money earmarked for other signings, after paying about £3m including bonuses. Flashscore reports Benfica hold a 20% sell-on and a right to match offers, and Varela’s agents meet Monza this week.

Yes, but in the summer and only if Gyokeres leaves. Arsenal’s results are strong, so a January rush for a 21-year-old would add risk without fixing a crisis. A fee near £26m looks modest beside the £64m Gyokeres cost, and Varela’s goals-per-game record argues for the gamble far more than Gyokeres’ two in 15 does.

The real risk is suitability. He also scores for a struggling side, so his chances come in games unlike most of the Premier League games Arsenal play. Arteta needs a number nine who presses and wins duels, and Varela does neither well, so Arsenal would be buying a finisher and building the rest of his game themselves.

That is workable if Varela arrives as competition for Havertz rather than the first choice. Arsenal should also expect resistance beyond the price, because Benfica’s matching right and Inter’s summer plans complicate any early bid.

Watching him until June costs Arsenal nothing, and another 20 league games will show whether this form is real or a hot streak.

#1463. Chelsea’s England playmaker on Man Utd’s radar

Chelsea transfer news around Cole Palmer has flared again, with Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival at Manchester United reviving the noise. Reporter Dean Jones insists the England playmaker’s future at Stamford Bridge is not in doubt, but he admits the sentiment around it is becoming harder to ignore.

Palmer, a boyhood United supporter, has been linked with Old Trafford before. United appointed Pochettino on 18 November after sacking Michael Carrick following one win in ten league games. The Argentine made Palmer one of his most used players at Chelsea, where the pair built a positive relationship, and Palmer scored 22 league goals in 2023/24.

Jones rates the chances of Palmer joining United as extremely low. United’s January budget stands at roughly £50m, and they want a left-back, a centre-back and a striker. A player FotMob values at €100m, roughly £87m, sits outside both the money and the shopping list. Jones also sees no sign that Palmer wants to leave, and says relations at Stamford Bridge would need to break down badly first.

Palmer has started all 11 of Chelsea’s Premier League games this season, playing 970 minutes for three goals, one from the penalty spot, and three assists. His 23 chances created include six big chances, and his 2.58 expected goals backs up the output. Xabi Alonso says, “The better Cole we have, the better Chelsea we have”.

Only ten of Palmer’s 31 shots have hit the target; he wins 46.9% of his dribbles, and he has collected two yellows and a red. Fitness worries more after an injury-hit 2025/26 that ended with him missing the World Cup.

No, but Chelsea should treat Jones’s condition as the real warning. Palmer’s contract runs to 2034, and United’s budget does not reach his valuation, so the danger lies in a deteriorating relationship, not a bid. That puts the onus on Alonso, Chelsea’s seventh permanent manager since 2021.

Morgan Rogers’ £117m arrival from Aston Villa creates the obvious flashpoint. If Palmer feels crowded out of the number ten role, or pushed wide right too often, the homesickness talk will return. Clear roles and managed minutes will protect him better than another forward.

The money belongs elsewhere. Alonso’s side beat United 2-0 on 31 October, then lost 1-0 at Sunderland eight days later, and defensive brittleness and thin squad depth keep undermining a front line that already scores. A back line that leaks goals will not.

#1462. GdS: ‘A chance for Jashari’ – what Amorim expects as Modric hands over the reins

Tomorrow evening, AC Milan will entrust Ardon Jashari with the job of filling Luka Modric’s shoes, after the Croatian’s injury.

If you missed last night’s reporting, Milan have been dealt a bit of a blow ahead of their game against Olympiacos, as Modric has suffered a muscle strain. It’s not a major one, and he should be back for next weekend’s game.

Nevertheless, it creates a short-term issue and in a midfield where only a few names have convinced, it plunges Ruben Amorim into the water somewhat. There is a solution, though, and it would be ideal if he stepped up.

Since he arrived, Jashari has been seen as the next in line for Modric, but he’s never shown performances to match that eventual rise. However, Gazzetta dello Sport (as seen below) write that he could take that step against Olympiacos.

It’s a potential turning point for the Swiss, who still has the faith of the club and the fans, especially after his first goal at the weekend. So, with it being a necessity that he comes into the team here, a solid performance is needed.

It opens a space for Jashari, but filling Modric’s boots will not be an easy task. In fact, he’ll have to be at his best to replace him, especially in a game with so much on the line.

Looking at the Europa League table, the Rossoneri need to be perfect if they’re to have any chance of a top eight finish. For him, though, Jashari must be perfect if his journey at San Siro is to continue.

So far, his time in Italy has been marred by injury and a failure to establish himself as a starter, or even a key rotational option. Yet, the Diavolo never gave up on him, refusing a sale in the summer.

Now, it is time to repay that in a game where ‘everything looks different’. For Jashari, it’s a simple task: be solid. He’s got a guaranteed place, reliable teammates around him and the trust to act.

No one can challenge him for the next five days; the spot is guaranteed. It’ll be up to him if those five days become 10 or more. If not, there’s a market waiting for him.

#1461. Liverpool lining up Ajax teenager for January

Liverpool transfer news from Goal says Ajax teenager Abdellah Ouazane is a January target as attacking cover for Florian Wirtz. Julian Ward, Liverpool’s recruitment chief, has reportedly sped up plans to support the £116m playmaker, and Ouazane has become a serious option before the winter window opens. Wael Mohya and Gilberto Mora sit on the same shortlist.

The 17-year-old grew up supporting Liverpool and badly wants to play at Anfield. Ajax hold the leverage, though: his contract runs to 2028, and persuading them to sell a prized academy graduate mid-season will take careful negotiation. De Telegraaf also reported earlier this season that sporting director Jordi Cruyff wants to give him a new deal when he turns 18 on 15 January.

Ouazane is mainly an attacking midfielder who also plays wide or up front. FotMob‘s 2026/27 numbers show two goals and one assist in 12 Eredivisie games, only four of them starts, across 441 minutes. His goals and shot attempts rank in the 88th and 86th percentiles among comparable attackers.

The gaps are just as clear: he sits in the 19th percentile for defensive contributions and the 15th for aerial duels won, and a 45.7% dribble success rate suggests he still loses the ball too often against senior opponents. Real Madrid pulled out of a 2025 deal after his medical, though Ajax’s own checks cleared him.

Iraola’s Liverpool press harder and play more direct than they did under Arne Slot, so that defensive profile matters. Wirtz works as the central creator with Bradley Barcola, Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha out wide, which leaves the number 10 role as Ouazane’s only route in.

Yes, but as a planned investment rather than genuine cover. Wirtz missed several matches with a back problem last February, so depth behind him is a fair concern. Yet Liverpool sit fourth, a point behind second-placed Brighton after Sunday’s 4-0 win over Manchester United, and only eighth in the Champions League table after losing to Fenerbahce. January minutes will decide those races, and Ouazane has four Eredivisie starts and numbers that clash with Iraola’s pressing.

His lifelong Anfield dream and Ward’s record of targeting elite teenagers give Liverpool an edge, so they should push. If Ajax demand a premium for a mid-season exit, Ward should wait for the summer, when Liverpool can judge a full Eredivisie campaign. Four starts make him a bet on 2028, not insurance for February.

#1458. Jude Bellingham backed to become England's greatest ever player amid Premier League 'travesty'

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 21:20

Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham has been tipped to become England's greatest ever player by former Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Jamie O'Hara, who believes the 23-year-old is already a better footballer than Harry Kane.

Bellingham produced another outstanding Champions League performance on Tuesday, scoring a spectacular goal and providing an assist in Real Madrid's 5-1 victory over PSV Eindhoven at the Bernabeu.

The England international improvised a remarkable volley with the outside of his boot after the ball bounced back towards him on the edge of the penalty area, later describing the strike as the best goal of his career.

His performance prompted an enthusiastic reaction from O'Hara, whose admiration for Bellingham is accompanied by a growing frustration that English football supporters have never had the opportunity to watch him regularly in the Premier League.

Speaking on talkSPORT's The Sports Bar, O'Hara made a bold prediction about Bellingham's international career.

"He's going to be England's greatest ever player. Ever. He's better than Harry Kane, a better player than Kane," the former Tottenham midfielder said.

Coming from a former Spurs player, the comparison carries weight given Kane's achievements for both club and country. England's all-time leading goalscorer has established himself as one of the finest centre-forwards of his generation, although Bellingham's influence on matches comes from a different position.

The Real Madrid midfielder has registered seven goals and five assists in 18 appearances across all competitions this season, with only Kylian Mbappe directly contributing to more goals for Los Blancos in La Liga.

His ability to influence proceedings from midfield while regularly producing decisive contributions in the final third makes him a valuable player for England. By the time Euro 2028 comes around, Bellingham should be approaching the peak years of his career, with considerable experience of European football already behind him.

O'Hara also described it as a "travesty" that Premier League supporters do not get to watch the midfielder in domestic action every week. However, fellow pundit Jason Cundy suggested that Bellingham's decision to develop his career outside England may have contributed to his success.

Unlike many of England's leading internationals, Bellingham has built his reputation almost entirely outside his homeland. He left Birmingham City for Borussia Dortmund in 2020 at the age of 17 before joining Real Madrid three years later.

His time in Germany allowed him to establish himself as a regular at Champions League level while still a teenager. At Madrid, he won both La Liga and the Champions League in his debut campaign, scoring 23 goals across all competitions.

The prospect of Bellingham eventually playing in the Premier League appears increasingly distant, with Real Madrid reportedly in advanced negotiations over a new long-term contract.

According to The Athletic, the Spanish giants intend to announce an agreement before the end of the calendar year, with Bellingham expected to receive a significant increase on his current annual salary of approximately £12.6m.

His existing deal already runs until June 2029, meaning Real Madrid are under little immediate pressure to negotiate. Their willingness to offer improved terms more than two and a half years before its expiry reflects the importance they attach to retaining the midfielder.

For England, there is little sporting reason to regret Bellingham's absence from the Premier League. He is developing at one of Europe's most demanding clubs and gaining experience in the latter stages of major competitions. The disappointment expressed by O'Hara is understandable from a spectator's perspective, but the Three Lions may benefit from the unconventional route their midfielder has taken.

#1455. Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Big Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters

Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 23 November 2026

Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.

Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.

One problem for Andoni Iraola is his side's frailties in the bigger games, which comes into focus this weekend with United in town – despite the desire to make an easy joke about how this is a clash against relegation fodder.

Since thrashing United 7-0 in 2023, Liverpool have beaten their friends in Manchester just once in seven meetings, including two draws and a defeat at Anfield.

To use a cliche, form seems to go out of the window for this fixture. In the last two Anfield meetings, Liverpool have been first and second in the table, United 14th and then tenth. This weekend, it is fourth against 18th, though Pochettino’s side could be bottom by kick-off.

Liverpool’s struggles in bigger games stretch further. Against the so-called 'Big Six’, the Reds have won just two of 12 games since winning the Premier League title. In a ‘mini league’ of those six sides, Liverpool are bottom in the aforementioned period.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side must prove on Sunday they can deliver in the biggest matches

Manchester United did the double over Liverpool in the Premier League last season

United did the double over Liverpool last season, Manchester City have beaten them four times in little over 12 months, Arsenal won on Merseyside a month ago.

So why has this team gone from looking formidable 18 months ago to rather flappable whenever the historic big boys are in town? Casual neutrals who only tune in for the showpiece Sunday 4.30pm may joke that they have not seen Liverpool play well for a good year.

A lot of the answer to that question comes back to Arne Slot and the issues we documented every week last season, when his side were dull and boring to watch, naked in defence and would capitulate in an instant.

Maybe players like Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola thrive more in intricate spaces rather than the gaping gaps left behind by the attack-minded bigger teams.

Another reason could be the simple fact that these sides are more likely to expose Liverpool’s vulnerabilities, such as the lack of a true defensive midfielder, the poor full backs or the frailties at defending set-pieces.

Anfield has lost its fear factor somewhat, too. Liverpool are top of the Premier League away table with 13 points from 15, but 18th in the home table with just one win in five games.

City had not won in front of a crowd there since 2003, now they have done it two seasons running. Arsenal had not triumphed at the stadium for 14 years until last month.

Iraola is aware of all this and said on Friday: ‘United finished third in the table last season. You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season.

Liverpool bemoaned Ryan Gravenberch’s red card in their home defeat to Manchester City

The Reds spurned a number of chances when they were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal last month

‘Now we have just started, this is just 10 games. So, for sure, they will be a lot higher in the table (soon). We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third.

‘We have to look at ourselves because we need the points. We need to improve our home form. It is also a big game in terms of relevance. It’s Liverpool v Manchester United, so we want to play well and we want to win.’

Asked if he understands the importance of the fixture to fans, Iraola – who spent the weekend off taking in grassroots football and netball games following his kids – said: ‘I am very aware! This is the biggest one in English football. In this country, this is the one.’

In Iraola’s first two bigger games, a theme threatened to emerge. Against Manchester City, Liverpool were well in the contest until Ryan Gravenberch’s red card but were toothless when it came to putting their chances away, lacking bite in attack.

The game was there to be won at 0-0, with the Anfield crowd roaring, but the Reds did not have the killer instinct to do so.

Against Arsenal, there were plenty of chances to equalise after the Gunners’ early goal but, again, goalkeeper David Raya could have put his feet up and had a cigar. A lot of territory but nothing to make the defence seriously sweat.

In both cases, Liverpool were on the receiving end of refereeing howlers. Gravenberch’s red was not a red – the first yellow should never be a booking – and Alexander Isak had a stonewall penalty turned down. ProRef has admitted errors.

To take a cynical view, though: in the title-winning campaign, we were rarely sat talking about referees or moaning about narrow misses or unfair results. Liverpool found ways to win and had no excuses.

Liverpool need Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to step up against the league's big boys

And that brings us nicely on to Sunday. It feels like the script has been written for weeks.

Indeed, after United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth and the score was read out to huge cheers at Anfield, Daily Mail Sport wrote: ‘Everyone is looking forward to United sacking Michael Carrick and then rocking up at Anfield to win 1-0 with their new manager in a few weeks.’

It always seems to happen and it feels like United get results against rivals Liverpool and City even when they have felt close to their lowest ebb.

But Liverpool and Iraola must not allow that to happen. There can be no excuses of ‘new manager bounce’, refereeing calls or fine margins come Sunday tea time.

Isak and Wirtz simply must step up. It feels harsh that the pair, Wirtz especially, are always in the spotlight but the £125million and £116million signings have flattered to deceive against the big boys.

Both have been spectacular at times this term but need to show up when it really matters, while £123million addition Barcola is still waiting for his first Premier League goal.

Iraola has history with United. As a player, his Athletic Club side beat Sir Alex Ferguson’s great side 5-3 over two legs in Europe.

‘I said at the time, it was one of the best wins of my career,’ he said. 'United, I remember, were champions of the Premier League, got to the Champions League final and lost to Barcelona the year before. We honestly played much better than them.’

Iraola has remained unbeaten against United into his managerial career, winning two and drawing four of his six meetings with them.

Overall, the former Bournemouth boss has played 38 games against ‘Big Six’ teams in the league: winning ten, drawing ten, losing 18.

But a win is all that matters on Sunday and it is a chance for Liverpool to set the tempo ahead of a busy festive schedule. After already taking on the current top three, Iraola now contests two rivalries with a trip across the city to Everton next week.

Six of nine pre-Christmas games are at Anfield so there is a real chance to build a head of steam in the league, qualify for the next stage of Europe and get to the Carabao Cup semi-final.

Iraola would welcome those festive gifts but, for Liverpool fans, nothing will be sweeter than giving their old foes a good old walloping on Sunday.

#1453. Koopmeiners scores at former club as Juventus beat AZ 2-1 despite trailing on expected goals

Juventus won 2-1 at AZ Alkmaar on a night when Teun Koopmeiners faced his old club, even though the hosts dominated the expected-goals count. The result strengthens their league-phase position ahead of Sunday's Serie A trip to Fiorentina.

The trip to Alkmaar returned Teun Koopmeiners to his former club. His brother Peer was in the AZ side that Juventus then held off. UEFA picked out the family meeting in its matchday 4 round-up.

Koopmeiners opened the scoring in the 19th minute from a Kolo Muani pass. Kolo Muani doubled the lead in the 37th minute, with Nick Woltemade credited with the assist, and Juventus led 2-0 at half-time. Kolo Muani earned a rating of 8.61 from the data provider, with Koopmeiners on 8.2.

AZ pulled one back in the 88th minute. Mexx Meerdink scored from an Elijah Dijkstra assist. The hosts could not find an equaliser in the remaining minutes.

The home side had 56% of possession. They completed 523 passes to Juventus’s 378. Eleven of AZ’s attempts were blocked, against three of Juventus’s.

Both teams put three shots on target. Vicario made two saves for Juventus. AZ’s expected goals total points to the chances the hosts created without converting them.

The figures are consistent with a Juventus side defending a first-half lead. Spalletti’s team committed 20 fouls to AZ’s 13. Andrea Cambiaso, Jeff Ekhator and Juan Cabal were booked for Juventus. Wesley Hoedt was the only AZ player shown a yellow card. Damian Sylwestrzak refereed the match.

The victory was Spalletti’s second in a row in all competitions, following the league win over Napoli. It came after a run that included a 0-2 defeat to Genoa and a 0-3 loss to Lazio. Koopmeiners now has four goals for Juventus in all competitions in 2026, one more than the three he scored for the club in 2025, Sky Sport Italia noted.

For AZ, the result was a third straight defeat in all competitions. Losses to Ajax and Twente came before Thursday’s game.

This season’s league phase has 36 clubs, and each plays eight different opponents. It ends on Thursday 28 January 2027. Juventus host Omonia Nicosia on 26 November at 21:00 CET, while AZ travel to Sparta Praha. Juventus then visit Hapoel Beer-Sheva on 10 December and Ferencváros on 21 January 2027, both at 18:45 CET. They finish at home to Real Sociedad on 28 January 2027 at 21:00 CET.

Serie A comes first. Juventus travel to Fiorentina for matchday 11 on Sunday 8 November, with kick-off at 20:45. AZ host Groningen in the Eredivisie on the same day.
